thread:
maria: FYI incoming from customer (ticket #5839). They report SSE stream stops abruptly ~1 token before the end, the JSON payload is left open and there's no finish_reason. Repro steps attached.
alex: Can you paste the raw stream capture? browser SDK or server-side?
maria: Customer ran curl from their backend. Here's the trimmed capture they sent (sanitized):\n\n```\nevent: response\ndata: {"choices":[{"text":"...final sentence starts but gets cut", "index":0, "logprobs":null},\n\n// connection closes here, no closing ] or }, no finish_reason\n```\n\nmaria: They also said this happened right after a billing plan change in their account, and they saw a 200 then silent EOF on the TCP socket.
tony: Hm. Two immediate hypotheses: 1) auth/billing state change triggered a proxy to reset the connection, 2) client reconnect resume header mismatch left an open kvcache state so server didn't emit final flusher. Can you confirm if they were doing resume (client provided resume headers)?
maria: Customer says they were NOT intentionally resuming — just a single long-stream generation. Token was rotated ~30s before the request (they use short-lived tokens).
alex: Ok. Please ask customer to re-run with this exact curl to collect raw bytes and Response headers (we need to see any intermediate 1xx/302/401):\n\n```bash\ncurl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\\n  -o - https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/streams/generate\n```\n\nalex: When they run, ask them to pipe output into a file and attach it (binary-safe). Also grab tcpdump/pcap if possible around the time.
maria: I've asked the customer for the raw file and pcap. They provided these hints:\n- socket closed client-side, no HTTP error code seen in app logs\n- server logs show request accepted and tokens consumed, but no explicit close event on the runtime side\n- they saw a spike in latency ~120s before the closure\n\ntony: Could be a proxy idle/billing reassign job (our cloud partner sometimes rebinds resources during plan swaps). Those jobs sometimes issue a TCP FIN without propagating a final SSE event. Engineering should check whether the runtime emits an explicit final object (finish_reason) before socket close, and whether we flush the trailing sentinel synchronously on plan-change hooks.
alex: I'll add an ingest-bot trace to the thread. @ingest-bot can you pull the runtime trace for request id the customer sent? (we got their request-id header in logs: r-9a7c3b)
ingest-bot: Collected traces for r-9a7c3b: request accepted -> batching -> dispatched to model shard -> token emission started -> last emitted token at t+18s -> NO final flusher invocation logged -> connection closed at t+19s (TCP FIN) -> no finish_reason event recorded.

alex: That lines up with the "final flusher not called" theory. Next steps:
1) SRE: check if any proxy (ingress) recorded a close reason or RST around t+19s. Look for HTTP/2 RST or 499 from nginx equivalent.
2) Runtime: add defensive flush on connection termination path to emit a minimal final object if possible (e.g., {"finish_reason": "connection_closed", "partial": true}).
3) DevEx: advise customers to enable keepalive and to capture raw SSE output on their side to avoid client-level truncation masking.
maria: Customer asked if this is a billing-related outage. Can we confirm whether billing changes trigger mid-request terminate? We should avoid saying yes/no until SRE confirms.
alex: Agreed. I'm triaging with SRE now. Also ask the customer to try one quick repro: run the same long prompt but include header `X-No-Plan-Swap: true` (we'll honor as a debug-only bypass for control plane jobs) so we can see if stream survives the windows around plan-change. If they can't, ask them to repro during an off-peak window and attach pcap.
tony: Also request their SDK version and whether any intermediate API gateway (CloudFront/CF) is present. Some gateways buffer and then drop trailing bytes on backend handoffs.
maria: Customer returned a raw file — there's an extra trailing comma just before the connection cut in one sample. I'll upload to the ticket.
alex: Trailing comma suggests server serialized an array but didn't close it. Could be our serializer crashed after emitting comma, or the process was killed by the orchestration agent during a rebind. SRE: check host-level OOM/eviction events around that timestamp.
mar ia: (typo) oops meant maria :eyes: the customer is running node 18 SDK with built-in reconnect. They reported the reconnect attempted and then created a second session which got a full response. So it's intermittent but reproducible when plan changes happen.
alex: Great actionable items. I'll file an internal incident note and assign to eng-runtime and eng-sre. Please keep ticket #5839 updated with raw files and pcap. Until we have fix, recommend customers use shorter streams or explicit final sentinel in the payload and client-side JSON repair (defensive parsing) as a workaround.
maria: Will do. Customer appreciated the quick triage. Closing loop when SRE/Runtime has root cause.
